gen_risks.description: Initial project execution and disbursements may be delayed due to national and subnational budget allocation and execution bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: GORE Arequipa will initiate budget allocation procedures immediately upon loan signing as prescribed in the Project Operational Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates

gen_risks.description: GORE Arequipa lacks experience implementing World Bank-financed operations, risking non-compliance with World Bank fiduciary, environmental, and social policies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) funds for advance PIU capacity building on Bank fiduciary, environmental, and social requirements prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: GORE... does not have experience implementing WB-financed projects, so capacity building and close supervision will be required

gen_risks.description: Severe weather events, heavy rainfall, flooding, and landslides linked to El Niño could damage access roads and interrupt construction and tourist mobility.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient engineering standards into road and infrastructure designs, including slope stabilization, reinforced drainage, and retaining walls.
gen_risks.evidence: floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations

gen_risks.description: Earthquake damage and disrepair in 17th-19th century churches could lead to structural failure or improper restoration during rehabilitation works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize traditional climate-resilient materials and structural reinforcement techniques supervised by specialized cultural heritage conservation guides.
gen_risks.evidence: The churches were built in the 17th to 19th centuries and are in various states of disrepair, many having suffered earthquake damage.

gen_risks.description: Delays in executing mandatory Interinstitutional Agreements with local municipalities will block loan disbursements for civil works under Components 1 and 2.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactively engage participating municipal authorities using GFPP resources to negotiate and execute required Interinstitutional Agreements prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made... for Parts/components 1 and 2... until and unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting qualified key staff for the PIU may delay project startup and impede operational efficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize terms of reference for all key PIU positions early and launch competitive recruitment to ensure appointments within 60 days of effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Delayed recruitment of FM staff... Terms of reference... shall be appointed within two months after effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation across sector ministries and local governments could cause conflicting priorities and implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize high-level Steering and Consultative Committees to formalize inter-institutional alignment between MINCETUR, MEF, MTC, Culture, and GORE.
gen_risks.evidence: Efficient budgeting and implementation of investments in tourism are hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape

gen_risks.description: Broader political instability and administrative changes in Peru could disrupt project decision-making and momentum.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an autonomous PIU structure reporting directly to the Governor and formalize binding multi-year interinstitutional commitments.
gen_risks.evidence: The slowdown has revealed important structural challenges... in addition to increased political instability in recent years.

gen_risks.description: Civil works and labor influx in rural tourism corridors create exposure to risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt and enforce a comprehensive SEA/SH Action Plan, worker codes of conduct, and accessible community grievance reporting channels.
gen_risks.evidence: exposure to sexual harassment and exploitation risks

gen_risks.description: High historical road fatality rates in Arequipa present safety risks for residents and visiting tourists along improved transport corridors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate comprehensive road safety features in road designs—such as speed calming, guardrails, markings, and pedestrian crossings—and perform safety audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Arequipa recorded 11.7 road traffic deaths per 100,000 people, a significantly higher rate than Peru's national average

gen_risks.description: Inadequate PIU experience with World Bank financial management procedures could result in accounting errors and delayed financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize the national SIAF system with SIAF-WB reconciliation controls, deliver early FM training, and retain independent external auditors.
gen_risks.evidence: Inadequate experience with Bank-financed projects may result in errors in financial records and reporting.

gen_risks.description: Global economic downturns, health crises, or regional travel disruptions could lower international tourism arrivals below project targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify destination promotion strategy to heavily target resilient domestic and South American regional markets alongside long-haul segments.
gen_risks.evidence: The pandemic has severely impacted the sector, and in 2025 Peru received 4.2 million international tourists, 78 percent of pre-pandemic levels.

gen_risks.description: Ambiguity in internal roles and operational procedures within the newly formed PIU could cause coordination failures and workflow delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define precise operational roles, internal control mechanisms, and decision workflows within the Project Operational Manual (POM).
gen_risks.evidence: Unclear internal coordination and roles within the PIU.

gen_risks.description: Uncontrolled grazing, agricultural encroachment, and wild forest fires threaten degradation of the delicate high-Andean Bosque de Queñua ecosystem.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute community-based forest monitoring, 174 ha of native reforestation, sustainable grazing technical assistance, and forest fire prevention training.
gen_risks.evidence: training and technical assistance related to grazing and agriculture management, prevention of illegal activities, prevention and control of forest fires

gt_risks.description: Peru is in a period of substantial political uncertainty (low popular support for the executive and Congress, high political fragmentation); a new government assumes office July 2026 and regional elections are scheduled October 2026. Since GORE Arequipa (a regional government) is the implementing agency, regional government changes could slow implementation or shift priorities; high-level changes at MINCETUR could also affect oversight commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focus on highly needed, consensus-driven investments; maintain buy-in and continuous dialogue with the tourism private sector; engage proactively with any new authorities on project opportunities; use implementation arrangements that are technically strong, highly competent, and relatively shielded from political influence and staff turnover.

gt_risks.description: Tourism projects are inherently complex, involving infrastructure, capacity building, and multiple government levels/sectors plus private-sector and community stakeholders. Capacity must be built at GORE Arequipa given no precedent for multisectoral regional investment programs in Peru, and historic national-regional coordination weaknesses. The project also does not budget for O&M of delivered sites/infrastructure, which falls to designated stakeholders.
gt_risks.mitigation: Institutional capacity building via the Project (incl. GFPP) to ready GORE for implementation; World Bank support on PIU composition and key staff selection; coordination arrangements/agreements between the PIU and local partners in charge of operating sites, to align on design, implementation, and handover.

gt_risks.description: Combined fiduciary risk with GORE Arequipa is Substantial, reflecting the entity's lack of prior experience with World Bank or other MDB-financed operations in both financial management and procurement.
gt_risks.mitigation: A fiduciary assessment identified capacity gaps and informed mitigation measures; recruit dedicated FM and Procurement Specialists supported by qualified administrative staff; detail minimum FM/procurement procedures aligned with WB requirements in the Project Operational Manual; use SIAF for financial transactions/reporting and STEP for procurement planning/monitoring; targeted WB training, regular fiduciary supervision, and annual audits.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk reflects the scope/nature of planned interventions, works located in environmentally and culturally sensitive areas, and GORE Arequipa's limited institutional capacity to manage risks per the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthen PIU capacity to manage E&S risks with adequate resources/staffing; elaborate and implement project-level instruments (Stakeholder Engagement Plan, Labor Management Plan, SEA/SH Plan) plus intervention-level instruments with specific mitigation measures.
